title: ICT, gender inequality, and income inequality: a panel data analysis across countries
decision_rationale: Quantitative cross-country panel (86 economies, 2013-2016) estimating ICT (mobile, internet, fixed broadband) effects on gender inequality and, via mediation, on Gini income inequality (family 4).
exposure_measure: Latent ICT construct (PLS) from mobile subscriptions per 100, % individuals using internet, fixed broadband subscriptions per 100 (Network Readiness Index reports); Table 1, p.715

sample.economies_or_groups: Appendix list p.723: e.g. Albania, Bangladesh, Ethiopia, Germany, US, Uganda, Vietnam
sample.income_groups_covered: mixed (high through low; developed vs developing contrast in post hoc)

design.estimator: PLS path modelling, cross-lagged evolution model, four waves (T1-T4) with separate path coefficients per year; bootstrapped 5000; multigroup analysis across time
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: Income inequality: GDP per capita (log), adult literacy, remittances, HDI. Gender inequality: democracy index, urban population growth, voice and accountability. No fixed effects.

results.indicator: Gini index (income inequality); indirect effect of ICT via gender inequality (mediation)
results.estimate: T1 -0.737; T2 -0.006; T3 -0.005; T4 -0.004 (standardized path coefficients)
results.evidence: Table 4, p.720: 'ICT (T1) -> Gender inequality (T1) -> Income inequality (T1) -0.737 0.000'. Only T1 is significant at 5%; T2-T4 are at 10% only, yet text says 'significant mediation across all four time periods' (p.716)

results.indicator: Gender inequality index (GII), effect of ICT (ICT is not linked directly to Gini)
results.evidence: Table 2, p.717; text 'ICT significantly reduces gender inequality ... for all time periods' though T2-T4 p>0.05

results.indicator: Gini index, effect of gender inequality (not ICT)

heterogeneity.finding: Development status (higher for developed) moderates gender inequality -> Gini effect only in T3 (0.076, p=0.008); T1 0.133 p=0.179; T2 0.093 p=0.179; T4 0.053 p=0.118. Moderation is of gender-Gini link, not ICT effect. Authors read it as stronger link in developed countries.
heterogeneity.evidence: Table 5, p.721; text p.717 'positive and significant moderation only for T3'

income_group_results.high: not reported separately; only continuous development-status moderator

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language (ICT 'impact', 'institutional enabler', policy advice to invest in ICT) but separate within-year paths; no country effects, instruments or lagged identification despite 'cross-lagged' label; reverse causation unaddressed.

exposure_measurement.why: Composite of mobile, internet, broadband captures ICT adoption reasonably, but weights and construct reliability not reported; authors concede ICT dimensions not fully captured.

selection_of_countries_years.why: Only four years (2013-2016); countries chosen by data availability; panel attrition acknowledged; 86 vs 85 inconsistency.

outcome_measurement.why: World Bank Gini and UNDP GII are standard but Gini is sparse and interpolated across countries/years; Gini described on 0-1 scale. Poor within-country comparability not discussed.

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: PLS with separate per-year coefficients, standardized betas with large T1 versus T2-T4 gap (-0.834 vs -0.030) suggest unstable or scale-driven estimates; ICT not in the Gini equation; different controls per equation; very high carry-over coefficients (~0.99) imply near-collinear waves.

selective_reporting.why: Interprets p of 0.054-0.099 as significant ('significant ... for all time periods'); mediation called significant at p=0.09-0.099; H1b and H2b non-support explained away. Hypotheses reported transparently in Table 6.
selective_reporting.evidence: Section 4 p.716; Table 4 p.720; Table 6 p.721

notes: Standardized PLS path coefficients are not elasticities; no direct ICT -> Gini coefficient is reported, only indirect via gender inequality. Table 3 contains apparent typos (e.g. '0.0991 < 0.994'), and the text cites 'Table 4' for the post hoc results (is Table 5) and 'H2b' where H1b is meant (p.719). No output or productivity outcome. No instructions embedded in text.
